title: Browse Medicare Part D prescription drug plans
summary: Overview of UnitedHealthcare Medicare Part D prescription drug plans, including benefits, coverage, enrollment periods, costs, and the AARP Medicare Rx Preferred and Rx Saver plans.

atoms.title: What a Medicare Part D plan is
atoms.question: What is a Medicare Part D plan?
atoms.text: A Part D plan is private insurance that offers prescription drug coverage. You can get a Part D plan by itself (PDP) to work with Original Medicare, or as part of a Medicare Advantage plan (MAPD).

atoms.title: Benefits common to UnitedHealthcare Part D plans
atoms.question: What benefits do UnitedHealthcare Part D plans include?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers prescription drug coverage through standalone plans (PDP) and as part of most Medicare Advantage plans (MAPD). All of them have these benefits: most Part D covered adult vaccines have a $0 copay, including the shingles vaccine; all Part D covered drugs have a $0 cost share in the Catastrophic Coverage stage; and a 1-month supply of covered insulin costs no more than $35. Members also have access to more than 60,000 pharmacies and can have prescriptions sent from Optum Home Delivery Pharmacy.

atoms.title: Who is eligible for a Part D plan
atoms.question: Who is eligible for a Medicare Part D plan?
atoms.text: Most people become eligible for Medicare coverage when they turn 65 or have a qualifying disability or medical condition. Anyone who has Medicare Part A, Part B or both is eligible to enroll in a prescription drug plan if they live in the plan service area.

atoms.title: What Part D plans cover
atoms.question: What do Part D plans cover?
atoms.text: Part D plans cover drugs on the plan's drug list (formulary) and most vaccines not covered by Medicare Part B. Original Medicare and Medicare Supplement (Medigap) insurance plans do not cover prescription drugs, but most Medicare Advantage plans do.

Does Medigap cover medications?

atoms.title: What Part D plans generally don't cover
atoms.question: What drugs are not covered by Part D?
atoms.text: Part D plans generally don't cover drugs prescribed for anorexia, weight loss, weight gain, fertility, erectile dysfunction, cosmetic purposes or hair growth. They also don't cover prescription vitamins and minerals, non-prescription drugs, or drugs already covered by Medicare Part A and Part B.

atoms.title: When you can enroll in a Part D plan
atoms.question: When can I enroll in a Medicare Part D plan?
atoms.text: You can enroll when you first become eligible for Medicare, during your Initial Enrollment Period (IEP). If you already have Medicare coverage, you can add, drop or change Part D coverage during the Annual Enrollment Period (AEP), October 15 to December 7, or during a Special Enrollment Period (SEP) for qualifying life events, with dates that vary.

atoms.title: Working past 65 and the Part D penalty
atoms.question: What happens to Part D if I work past age 65?
atoms.text: If you choose to work past 65 and delay Part D enrollment, you may be subject to a Part D late enrollment penalty. You can avoid this penalty if you can show that you have creditable coverage equal to or better than a Part D plan.

atoms.title: AARP Medicare Rx Preferred vs Rx Saver
atoms.question: How do AARP Medicare Rx Preferred and Rx Saver differ?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers two Part D plans; availability may depend on where you live. AARP Medicare Rx Preferred has a $130 annual deductible for drugs in tiers 3, 4 and 5, a national and U.S. Territories service area, a Premium drug list, and a $0 copay at Optum Home Delivery for a 90-day supply of Tier 1 and 2 drugs. AARP Medicare Rx Saver has a $615 annual deductible, a national service area, a Standard drug list, and a $6 copay for a 90-day supply of Tier 1 generics at Optum Home Delivery. Rx Saver is suggested for people who receive Extra Help or want a robust pharmacy network.

atoms.title: 2026 Part D deductible limit is $615
atoms.question: What is the Part D deductible limit for 2026?
atoms.text: Standalone Part D plans charge a monthly premium and may also have an annual deductible, copays and coinsurance. For plans with an annual deductible, the 2026 limit set by Medicare is $615.

atoms.title: Part D cost sharing: copay and coinsurance
atoms.question: How does cost sharing work for Part D prescriptions?
atoms.text: When you fill a prescription for a covered drug, you may need to pay a copayment (a set amount) or coinsurance (a percentage). Amounts vary based on what tier the drug is in and what pharmacy you use. Total costs also vary with the number of prescription drugs you need, how often you take them, whether you use a network pharmacy and what coverage stage you are in. Your costs may be lower if you qualify for the Extra Help program.

atoms.title: The Part D coverage stages
atoms.question: What are the Part D coverage stages?
atoms.text: Part D costs depend on the coverage stage. In the Deductible stage, if your plan has one, you pay the full cost of your prescriptions. In the Initial Coverage stage, you pay a copay or coinsurance. In the Catastrophic Coverage stage, the plan pays the full amount for Medicare covered Part D drugs.
